goal: Test whether a probability model trained only on other migrated surveys can adapt causally to a new Waka stream, while clearly separating later-tile performance from charged startup cost.

cross_survey_base.training: Kahu + Opunake only; zero Waka training

same_hard_tile_causal_adaptation.rule: score each already-causal trace/chunk before updating; encoder and decoder can reproduce the same updates
same_hard_tile_causal_adaptation.note: This uses no earlier Waka tile but only modestly improves transfer.

broader_universal_model.training: diverse Kahu + Opunake + Tui tiles; zero Waka in pretrained weights

later_hard_tile_after_two_already_decode.warning: Later-tile diagnostic only. Do not present as whole-stream rate because the two Waka calibration tiles are not included in this number.

interpretation: The learned waveform-shape mechanism is substantially cross-survey transferable after decoder-reproducible adaptation. The main remaining penalty is cold-start/startup cost on a new survey, not failure to adapt. The honest three-tile charged diagnostic is currently about 1.59x vs SZ3, while later tiles can reach about 1.64x under the stricter charged-prefix experiment and about 1.69x in a stronger later-tile-only prefix diagnostic. None is a 2x or serialized-codec claim.
next: Reduce cold-start cost with deterministic fast adaptation from the earliest decoded blocks.
Measure leave-one-survey-out adaptation on Kahu, Opunake and Tui, not just Waka.
Only after ideal rate is comfortably below the 2x target, materialize the arithmetic stream and benchmark throughput.
